findings.title: Cached login IDPs bypass the org enabled check for REALM_ONLY callers
findings.body: Cached results are returned from getById, and those models are wrapped so that isEnabled also checks the linked organization. Disabling an organization does not invalidate the login cache keys, so cached lists can still contain IDPs of a disabled org. Only the ORG_ONLY and ALL callers re-check isEnabled. Any other caller of getForLogin, such as the base IdentityProviderBean or third-party code, will now receive IDPs that are effectively disabled. The cache should either filter by isEnabled before returning, or the organization enable/disable path should invalidate the login cache keys.

findings.title: Login cache invalidation on update misses changes that alter list membership
findings.body: Invalidation is skipped when the IDP qualifies for login both before and after the update with the same organization. Changes that the predicate does not cover can still affect the cached results, for example the delegate's search semantics like a null orgId match. In addition, `idpById` is the org-aware wrapper whose isEnabled depends on the organization state, while `updated` is not wrapped. The two sides of the comparison can therefore disagree, so the cache can be wrongly skipped or wrongly invalidated.

findings.title: Cleanup removes literal alias "alias" instead of created IDPs
findings.body: `get("alias")::remove` refers to a non-existent IDP, so none of the 21 created IDPs is cleaned up. They leak into other tests that run in the same realm.
